...for the respondent/Insurance Co.
The instant appeal has been preferred against the judgment and award dated 26th February, 2021 passed by learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, FTC-3, Berhampore, Murshidabad, in MAC Case no. 184 of 2014.

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case is that the present appellants being the claimants have preferred an application before the learned tribunal under Section 166 of the M.V. Act for getting compensation on the ground that their predecessor was died in a road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle duly insured under the policy of the Insurance Company.
The claim case was contested by the Insurance Company before the learned tribunal by filling written statement.

After hearing the parties and after receiving the evidences the learned tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 32,66,960/- in favour of the claimants and direct to the Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said award the present appeal has been preferred by the claimants for enhancement of the compensation.

The ground of enhancement as argued by Mr. Rahaman, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants is that the learned tribunal has deducted 1/3rd of the compensation towards his personal expenses.
By virtue of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma while the number of claimants are 4 the deduction towards the personal expenses would be 1/4th.
In this case, the claimants are the widow, minor son and daughter and the mother of the deceased.

So, in this case Tumpa Saha & Ors vs National Insurance Company Ltd. & Anr on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101044084/

sentences.text: the applicable multiplier would be 1/4th instead of 1/3rd.
He further argued that the deceased was a school teacher and according to the admit card his date of birth is 2nd of July, 1971.
The alleged accident happened on 16.12.2013; at the time of accident the deceased was 41 years of age.
According to the observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma.
The applicable multiplier would be 14.
But, the learned tribunal as adopted the multiplier to be 10 which is without a basis.
He further argued that the deceased was a teacher of a Government School.
So, he was engaged in a permanent job.
So, the claimants are entitled to get the future prospects which would be 30% to the actual salary of the deceased.
On the ground, he argued that the award passed by the learned tribunal need be modified.
Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Insurance Company submits that the learned tribunal has awarded the compensation on the basis of the factual matrix of this case.
The learned tribunal has considered entire facts and circumstances of this case and has correctly decided the issue.

He further argued that the claimant has already received the entire awarded amount so after receiving the awarded amount it is quite improper for the appellant to file the appeal for the enhancement of compensation.
So, he prayed for dismissal of the instant appeal.
Heard the learned advocates perused the materials on records also considered the observation of the learned tribunal in this case.
It appears that the number of the claimants are four so in this case the deduction towards the personal expenses of the deceased, had he been alive, would be 1/4th instead of 1/3rd.
The original admit card of the deceased was placed in LCR.
On perusing the admit card of Madhyamik Examination it appears that the date of birth of the deceased is 02.07.1971.
So, it appears that the deceased was 41 years of age at the time of accident.
Accordingly, the applicable multiplier would be 14.
It further appears that the learned tribunal has erroneously fixed the general damages.
The general damages in a case under Section 166 of the M.V. Act shall be as per direction of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi.
Deceased was the permanent teacher of the Government School.
So, the claimants are entitled to the future prospects which would be 30% actual salary of the deceased.
Considering the same, it appears that the award passed by the learned tribunal need be modified.

The just and proper compensation of this case assessed as hereunder:-
Calculation of compensation 1.

Monthly Salary :Rs.39,712/-
2. Yearly Income :Rs.4,76,544/-
3.

Add: 30% Future prospects :Rs.1,42,963/-
Rs. 6,19,507/-
4. Multiplier 14 (Rs.4,64,634 X 13):Rs.65,04,834/-

 Balance to Pay :Rs.32,37,874/-
After calculation the just and proper  compensation comes to Rs.65,74,834/-.
The Insurance Company has already paid by virtue of the direction of the learned tribunal which has been already received by the claimants amounting to Rs.32,66,960/-.
The balance award comes to Rs. 32,37,874/-.

The Insurance Company is directed to pay the balance awarded sum alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application i.e. from 24.4.2014 till the date of already deposit made by the Insurance Company before the learned tribunal.

The Insurance Company is further directed to deposit the balance awarded sum alongwith the interest as mention above to the office of the learned tribunal within eight weeks from the date of passing of this order vide four equal account payee cheques.

On such deposit the claimant No. 1 shall receive the cheque of minor claimant Nos. 2 and 3 as their behalf as their natural guardian mother, and shall deposit in the name of the claimants No. 2 and 3 in a short term fixed deposit scheme under a Nationalized Bank so that the award may be utilized by the minors after the attainment of their majority.
The claimant No. 1 is further directed to deposit a copy of such bank account before the learned tribunal.
The award of compensation is subject to the ascertainment of payment of deficit Court fees, if any.
It appears that the LCR has already been received.
Department is directed to return the LCR promptly to the office of the learned tribunal for the proper compliance of this order.
The instant FMA 869 of 2022 is disposed of.
All connected applications, if any, stand disposed of.
Interim orders, if any, stand vacated.
Parties to act upon the server copy and urgent certified copy of this order be provided on usual terms and conditions.

(Subhendu Samanta, J.)
